subject: Embeddings migration & batching follow-up
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jacob Reynolds <jreynolds@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-10T15:12:00-08:00
Subject: Embeddings migration & batching follow-up

Hi Jacob -

Thanks again for the call today. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we’re aligned:  

Summary of needs:  
- You’re currently using ProviderX embeddings (768-dim) for product search + recommendations.  
- Goal: migrate to Redwood embeddings and the Redwood vector stack (ANN + reranker) to reduce latency and cost while preserving/recovering relevance.  

Technical notes / recommendations (high level):  
- Embedding model & dimensionality: Redwood’s recommended production embedding for this workload is the 1536-dim model (better semantic coverage for retail catalogs). If you want parity with existing vectors, we can discuss a 768-dim alternative or a projection approach, but re-embedding is generally recommended for best-quality migration.  
- Normalization: use unit (L2) normalization and cosine similarity for nearest-neighbor; this avoids scale issues and plays nicely with ANN indices.  
- Batching: we typically recommend batching ~256-512 documents per request depending on average tokenized size. For very long product descriptions chunk at ingestion then aggregate via centroid.  
- Migration strategy: option A = re-embed entire corpus (recommended for accuracy); option B = run a lightweight mapping layer (not lossless) + A/B test on a subset to measure R@k / MRR impact.  
- Reranker / structured output: keep your current sparse+embed retrieval pipeline and add a lightweight reranker (cross-encoder) for top-N re-ranking to preserve precision on SERP. Redwood supports a reranker step in the pipeline.  

Next steps I propose:  
1) Engineering kickoff: 30-45m migration scoping call (data volume, avg doc length, SLOs).  
2) Pilot: Re-embed a 10k-item seed set, build ANN index, run offline eval vs current vectors (MRR / precision @10).  
3) Rollout plan: staged migration by product category with canary traffic and fallback to ProviderX results if drift is observed.  

I attached the short post-call notes and a rough MVP arch diagram. I’ve included Vivek on the thread to help with batching/throughput estimates and Nikhil for any low-level migration questions.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.ai

Thanks Marissa - very helpful summary. A couple quick follow-ups from our eng team:  

1) Dimensionality question: ProviderX vectors are 768-dim. If we re-embed we’ll get 1536-dim vectors. What’s the recommended path for matching historical signals (clicks/conversions) that were trained against the old vectors? Is there a reliable projection approach or do you recommend nightly re-embedding of all historical items and retraining downstream models?  

2) Batching/throughput: we have ~2.5M SKUs; average description is ~120 tokens. Can you confirm a ballpark for time to embed the full corpus (assuming Redwood dedicated throughput, and a 1536-dim model)? Also any constraints on max batch size / token limits we should plan for?  

3) Re-ranking: we want to keep cost reasonable - if we do a top-50 ANN retrieval and then a cross-encoder rerank, what are typical latency/cost tradeoffs?

Can Vivek or someone from infra chime in on throughput estimates? Happy to schedule the pilot call.

Jacob

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Jacob Reynolds <jreynolds@acmeretail.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>, Nikhil Sharma <nikhil@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-01-12T11:37:00-08:00
Subject: Re: Embeddings migration & batching follow-up

Hi Jacob - great questions. I pulled some notes from Vivek/Nikhil below; posting them inline so you have a clear recommendation set.  

Dimensionality & historical signals:  
- Short answer: re-embedding historical items is the most robust approach for preserving/recovering downstream model quality. It avoids mismatch between vector spaces and ensures your relevance signals remain meaningful.  
- Projection/mapping options exist (learned linear projection from 768 -> 1536), but they typically lose fine-grained semantic detail and introduce noise; they are useful for short-term fallbacks or when re-embedding is infeasible. If you try projection, we recommend validating on a labeled holdout (MRR / CTR).  
- For retraining downstream models (e.g., conversion models using embeddings): do a staged retrain where the pilot set retrains and you monitor lift before full retrain.

Batching & throughput (Vivek):  
- With Dedicated capacity (N gpus), practical throughput for embeddings ingestion at 1536-dim: ~5k-20k docs/sec depending on GPU type and doc length. For 2.5M SKUs (~120 tokens avg) we estimate 4-14 hours end-to-end on a 4-GPU dedicated pool (this includes network/IO and index writes). We’ll size precisely during kickoff.  
- Recommended batch size: 256-512 docs/request. Avoid very large batches (>2k) since tokenization memory can spike and latency per-batch degrades.  
- Chunking: for long descriptions split at ~512 tokens and create one embedding per chunk then aggregate (centroid) at index time.

Normalization & similarity:  
- Use L2/unit normalization + cosine similarity for ANN. That’s the simplest and most stable. Redwood’s ANN stack (FAISS-based) uses normalized vectors by default for cosine.

Reranker tradeoffs (Nikhil):  
- Typical pattern: ANN (top-100) -> lightweight cross-encoder rerank (top-10 or top-20). This keeps cost down while recovering precision.  
- Latency: ANN retrieval is sub-10ms for typical shard sizes; cross-encoder depends on model size - a small cross-encoder (~base transformer) adds ~30-80ms per query; batching rerank requests for multi-query flows helps.  
- Cost: expect reranker CPU/GPU cost to be a minority if you only run it on top-N; rework thresholds if cost becomes dominant (e.g., only rerank queries above a confidence threshold).

Migration options & pilot scope:  
- Pilot: re-embed a 10k-50k slice representing top categories, build ANN index, run offline eval vs current embeddings, and A/B the reranker config.  
- Export/import: Redwood can export vectors and metadata if you’d like an offline snapshot for retraining.  

I’ve added two links: a short migration guide and a HubSpot deal link. Happy to get a migration kickoff on the calendar - Vivek, can you propose 2x time slots for next week?

Best,
Marissa
